root_motivation: An agent iterating on its own tools (visions/mcp-host.md addendum 2026-09-18, leaf 3) publishes, calls, fixes, and republishes -- today a republish overwrites the previous source outright (kinds/python.rs:41's on_tool_changed rebuilds the env and discards it, no version_history/tool_version concept anywhere in src), so a worse fix leaves the agent nothing to go back to, and a sharer of that tool (src/sharing.rs) sees the change with no warning and no way to pin. This PRD makes every publish an immutable, numbered version kept per plan, host.tool_rollback restores one in a single call, and a caller may pin a shared tool to a version so the owner's own iteration doesn't break it out from under them.
user_persona: Three (PRD User stories): (1) the owner calls host.tool_rollback {name, version: 3} to make version 3 current again after a bad republish; (2) the owner calls host.tool_history {name} to see every version with its timestamp and source hash before deciding what to roll back to; (3) a sharer pins {name, version: 3} on a cross-tenant call and keeps working unaffected while the owner iterates, with an unpinned sharer instead getting a one-time version_changed note in its result envelope.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a tool published twice, When host.tool_history is called, Then two versions are listed, version 2 current, with distinct source_sha256.
Given version 2 current, When host.tool_rollback {version: 1} is called, Then the next host.tool_call runs version 1's source.
Given a free tenant with 5 versions, When a sixth is published, Then version 1 is deleted and versions 2-6 remain.
Given host.tool_rollback {version: 9} for a tool with 2 versions, When called, Then an argument error names the valid range.
Given a shared tool at version 3 and a caller pinning version: 2, When the owner publishes version 4, Then the pinned call still runs version 2.

Given prod after ship, When homeward's tool is republished and rolled back once during the build's live check, Then host.tool_history on prod shows both versions (proof: the live call output in the trailer).

Per the PRD's own mock_justifications, the live check is written and ready for the operator's post-ship run at tests/mcphost_tool_versions_ac06_live_rollback_trailer.rs (gated on MCPHOST_LIVE=1) -- same convention as PRD-mcphost-uptime-probes/PRD-mcphost-team-memory's own AC6/AC8, not built in this coder dispatch since AC6 is outside this build's non-deferred AC list.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given an unpinned sharer, When the owner rolls back, Then the sharer's next result carries version_changed once and not on the following call.
Given host.tool_remove, When called, Then all versions are gone and host.tool_history returns not-found.
Given two versions, When host.tool_diff is called, Then a unified diff is returned.

additional.no_new_dependency_for_diff: host.tool_diff (P2/AC9) needs a unified diff of two spec JSON blobs; rather than add a diff crate for one small feature, src/difftext.rs hand-rolls a standard LCS line diff -- the same 'hand-roll when it's small and self-contained' call plans.rs's TOML writer and state.rs's RFC 3339 math already make in this crate.
additional.version_numbering_never_reused: tools.current_version is a POINTER (rollback can move it backward), not a counter -- the next version number a publish issues is MAX(version)+1 over that tool's own tool_versions rows (never the pointer), which stays correct across a rollback because retention only ever prunes the OLDEST surviving rows, never the highest version number ever issued.
additional.source_sha256_is_over_the_whole_spec: source_sha256 hashes the canonical (default serde_json::Value, so deterministically key-sorted) serialized spec JSON, not a kind-specific 'source' field -- echo/http specs have no such field at all, so a kind-agnostic hash is the only one that works for every kind uniformly.
additional.version_changed_scoped_to_cross_tenant: requirement 6's own wording ('a shared tool's unpinned caller') scopes the version_changed note to cross-tenant calls (caller.is_some() in call_published_tool) -- an owner's own unpinned host.tool_call after its own rollback never gets a version_changed note, since the owner already knows it just rolled back.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does one wrong republish break a running workflow for the owner and every sharer, with no undo short of pasting old source from a transcript?
five_whys_trace.a: kinds/python.rs:41's on_tool_changed rebuilds the sandbox env and discards the old source on every republish -- there is no version_history/previous_version concept anywhere in src (confirmed: grep -rniE 'tool_version|previous_version|version_history' src finds nothing before this PRD).

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't a sharer just re-fetch the tool by name after a bad republish to see what changed?
five_whys_trace.a: sharing.rs lets a caller reach an owner's tool by name with no version at all -- the caller has no way to even know a republish happened, let alone reach the version it depended on.

five_whys_trace.q: Why version the whole tools row (kind + spec together) rather than just the source text?
five_whys_trace.a: A spec isn't always just source -- echo/http specs have no 'source' field at all -- so tool_versions stores each publish's whole (kind, spec) pair; source_sha256 is computed over the canonical serialized spec JSON, kind-agnostically, for the same reason.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is the next version number MAX(version)+1 over tool_versions rather than current_version+1?
five_whys_trace.a: current_version is a POINTER a rollback can move backward (e.g. from 6 to 1) -- if the next publish's version number were current_version+1, a publish right after that rollback would try to insert version 2, colliding with the UNIQUE(tenant_id, name, version) constraint on the version 2 row retention never deleted. MAX(version)+1 stays correct because retention only prunes the OLDEST surviving rows, never the highest version number ever issued.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a version-pinned call need a reserved 'version' key inside the wire call-args object for the cross-tenant <owner_ns>.<name> path, instead of a cleaner sibling parameter?
five_whys_trace.a: Confirmed against handler.rs's call_tool dispatch: a direct <owner_ns>.<name> tools/call has no side channel beyond the wire arguments object itself (unlike host.tool_call, whose RPC params already have name/args/async as siblings) -- version has to be a reserved key inside that same object, stripped before schema validation/dispatch, the same shape this codebase's own tenant_key argument (PRD-mcphost-session-key) already uses for an analogous problem.

'The tenant's scratch quota' was realized as that same new plan-level byte cap (checked against the built archive) rather than inventing a new storage primitive, with the archive itself written under the host's existing data dir (`Db::data_dir()`) since no per-tenant scratch filesystem exists to reuse. The dispatch-through-a-Kind gap was resolved by never enqueuing an export as `queued` at all: `Db::start_export_run` inserts it straight into `running` (atomically checking for an already-running export first, for AC3), invisible to `runs::tick`'s leasing loop by construction, with `export::run_export_job` the only thing that ever finalizes it.

ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Fixed in place, same 'amend the paper trail without reopening the contract' pattern used for every prior recurrence: no reviewer block yet, but the same staleness would recur if left byte-for-byte. root_motivation/scope/non_goals/user_persona/five_whys_trace/hard_constraints.additional were rewritten from this PRD's own Problem statement, Goals, Requirements, Non-goals, and Technical considerations sections; acceptance_criteria's nine entries point at the real tests/mcphost_tool_versions_ac0[1-5,7-9]_*.rs files (AC1-5, AC7-9 exist, compile, and pass; AC6 is Live/operator-provisioned, deferred, same convention as every prior PRD's own Live AC in this card's history -- not built in this coder dispatch since the dispatch's own non-deferred AC list omits it entirely). agent/test-map.json's ac_test_map was repointed to this PRD and the prior uptimeprobes mapping preserved under ac_test_map_by_prefix (newly archived there) rather than deleted. On the three build-time decisions: (1) migration 0028's tool_versions table stores one `spec` TEXT column (the tool's whole JSON spec, exactly like `tools.spec` already does) plus `kind`, rather than inventing a source/config/requirements split this codebase has no other precedent for -- source_sha256 hashes that same canonical spec JSON, kind-agnostically. (2) resolved by treating `version` as a reserved key inside the cross-tenant call's own wire arguments object (stripped before schema validation/dispatch), the same shape `tenant_key` already uses for an analogous problem in this exact call path (see five_whys_trace above); `host.tool_call`'s own RPC params (which DO have a name/args/async sibling shape) get a real sibling `version` parameter instead, since that path has room for one. (3) scoped to cross-tenant calls only (`caller.is_some()` in `call_published_tool`), per requirement 6's own 'a shared tool's unpinned caller' wording -- an owner's own unpinned `host.tool_call` after its own rollback never gets a `version_changed` note, since `host.tool_call` only ever resolves the caller's OWN tools (there is no `caller` tenant distinct from the tool's owner on that path at all).
